expect.note: live_judge() with no OPENROUTER_API_KEY raises JudgeError naming the key, before any network call could occur

provenance: M36 acceptance criterion 2 (missing key). This environment genuinely has no OPENROUTER_API_KEY (a stated M36 environment constraint), so the probe needs no mocking: `src/browser/judge.py`'s `live_judge()` must raise `JudgeError` with 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY' in the message, the same shape `live_planner()` already uses in planner.py for the identical situation. Watched red against a version of `live_judge` that checked the key AFTER a cache miss but still attempted the HTTP call anyway would hang or raise a bare `urllib` error with no actionable message and, worse, would not be distinguishable from a real transient network fault -- the case pins the SPECIFIC, recognisable failure mode a caller can act on.

triage.note: one half of the fail-closed acceptance criterion; judge-fail-closed-on-error covers the OTHER half (an exception from an otherwise-configured judge, mid-run, through the real pipeline).
